speaker: Doctor

The description of a "fixed" and painless supraclavicular lymph node is highly concerning for malignancy rather than infection. Given your age and the severity of your "B symptoms," have you experienced any difficulty swallowing, hoarseness, or a persistent cough?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Work: Complete Blood Count - WBC: Elevated, Hemoglobin: Slightly Decreased, Platelets: Normal; Lactate Dehydrogenase: Elevated. Imaging: Chest X-Ray - Findings: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work and chest X-ray showing massively enlarged lymph nodes in the axillary, mediastinal, and cervical regions, combined with elevated LDH and your "B symptoms," are highly suggestive of a systemic lymphoproliferative disorder. Have you noticed any skin changes, such as itching or rashes, or have you experienced any bone pain recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma).

The constellation of B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), fixed supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, massively enlarged mediastinal and axillary nodes on imaging, elevated LDH, and abdominal fullness is diagnostic for an aggressive systemic lymphoma. The absence of cough and recent travel further reduces the likelihood of tuberculosis.
